data.body:
[P2] Renew the hold at actual invocation boundaries

`TestExecutionOrchestrator.isBusy()` includes queued functions and `timedCompletionReleased`, so it remains true when a wait or callback queues a wakeup before the running invocation ends. This reset is therefore skipped, and the next invocation inherits the previous invocation's expired hold. If the resumed child starts a durable wait alongside sub-second I/O, processing that wait can immediately advance to its caller's later deadline, corrupting ordering before the new invocation receives its one-second allowance. Reset the hold using an invocation ID or explicit lifecycle notification, and add a composed regression with a wakeup queued before the preceding invocation ends; manually toggling the unit-test participant to idle does not cover this transition.
